newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Mosel Jan-Sept profit down.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Mosel Jan-Sept profit down.

text.p: Mosel Vitelic Inc, one of Taiwan's leading chip makers, said its net profit for the first nine months of 1996 fell to T$3.289 billion from T$4.95 billion in the same period in 1995.
From January to September, the firm's sales revenue dropped to T$8.56 billion from T$9.43 billion in January-September 1995, Mosel said in a statement.
In September alone, Mosel posted net profit of T$277 million on sales of T$880 million, down from T$800 million and T$1.887 billion in September 1995.
In August, Mosel slashed its 1996 net profit forecast to T$4.029 billion from T$8.268 billion, and its sales forecast to T$12.259 billion from T$18.442 billion.
It was the second time in 1996 that Mosel had lowered both estimates. Mosel slashed its initial 1996 profit forecast of T$15.14 billion to T$8.268 in late April.
The company has attributed its earnings squeeze to freefalling prices of its main product, dynamic random access memory chips, since early 1996.
